# The document — canonical structure

One file: `evals/week_x_posts_<YYYY-MM-DD>.md`, dated the **Monday the week
opens**. Never overwrite a previous week's file; the series is the record.

The document has two jobs. It proposes the posts, and it **shows its work** so the
operator can disagree with the reasoning rather than just the wording. Sections
§0–§4 are the argument; the day-by-day is the deliverable; §8–§11 are the
operating manual.

---

## Header

```
# Week of X Posts — <N> posts, Mon <D> <Mon> → Sun <D> <Mon> <YYYY>

**Window:** … · 6 slots/day · **4 generated by me + 2 yours (14:00 & 21:00, manual)**
**Objective:** verified home-timeline impressions, not raw views. <one line on why it matters this week>
**Audience:** indie hackers, solopreneurs, AI builders. Every subject below is AI, the niche, or a live build-in-public controversy.
**Source:** <harvests with n and capture timestamps> for the *mechanism*; <news sources with dates> for the *subjects*.
**Format:** no links (invariant #1 — a URL bills $0.20 vs $0.015), no hashtags, no media. Every proposition on its own line, blank line between. All ≤280 chars.
```

The **Source** line is load-bearing: it is the first thing that separates this
from a model improvising tweets. Name the accounts, the n, and the capture time.

---

## §0 — Read this first

The state of measurement, stated before anything else.

- Can last week be scored? If not, **why**, how many originals are now ungraded,
  and the exact 60-second fix. If this is the second or third consecutive week,
  say so — the number going up is the argument.
- If it *can* be scored: the scoring table, and last week's §10 questions answered
  one at a time. This section becomes the most valuable in the document the moment
  own-post data exists.
- Any **hand-swap** the operator made to last week's queue, reported neutrally.

Never pad this section to hide a gap. A document that admits what it couldn't
measure is trusted; one that doesn't is astrology.

## §1 — What the harvest says about SHAPE

The skeleton buckets, as a table, with n and reply:like. Then:

- **The headline finding** in one bolded sentence with its numbers.
- **Outlier discipline made visible** — if a bucket was carried by one post, both
  numbers, and what that means for how much weight it gets.
- **Why the winning skeleton works**, as numbered mechanics, not adjectives.
- **The length accounting** — per-stream medians. If the set got longer than last
  week's, say so and explain the mix change. Never claim tightening that didn't
  happen.
- **What you're not taking, and why** — the shapes measured well and rejected
  anyway (link farm, milestone, borrowed catchphrase). Rejecting a measured winner
  on objective grounds is a stronger signal of judgement than picking one.

## §2 — The spine

The one through-line the week's events share, and where it gets said out loud.
Also: how many posts use the operator's age as warrant, and the argument that each
one earns it.

## §3 — What's actually live in the niche right now

Numbered live threads, each with **a date, a number and a `→ tag` mapping** to the
posts that use it. Example shape:

> **1 · OpenAI cut Cursor off. Yesterday.** SpaceX closed its $60B acquisition
> Aug 15; on Aug 29 OpenAI announced it is ending Cursor's model access … 824
> points and 516 comments on Hacker News. **→ N1, X1.**

Every peg dated. Every peg checkable by the reader in ten seconds. Undated
"people are saying" material does not belong here.

## §4 — The rules

R1–R10 from `mechanics.md` §3, restated compactly, plus any rule this week added.
A new rule needs the evidence that produced it in the same line.

## §5 — The slot grid

The table from `SKILL.md` Step 5, plus: slot-quality ordering, the gap structure,
the DST note if the week crosses Oct 25, and the collision check against the
previous week's tail.

## §6 — The rotation

| Stream | Count | What it is | Evidence |

Counts must sum to N. The Evidence column carries n and reply:like — that is what
justifies the count. Name any stream retired this week and why.

## §7 — Novelty and copy risk

- **Retired:** every subject, device and latch fired in the last 14 days,
  including pending rows. Dense prose is fine; completeness is the point.
- **Collisions caught**, with the fix. A shape that already fired in a different
  costume is the one readers notice.
- **Copy risk, stated plainly.** If a post shares a skeleton with a harvested
  account's post, say which, say why it is still yours, and park it off a marquee
  slot.

## §8–§11

- **§8 · Bench** — 4–5 swap-ins, each with the condition that fires it.
- **§9 · How to run it** — seed discipline, which streams to answer replies on,
  N-stream shelf life, reruns, spike protocol, expected yield. From
  `mechanics.md` §7, tailored to this set.
- **§10 · What to measure next Monday** — 2–4 falsifiable questions **in order of
  what they would change**, each with the decision it drives ("if X beats D, the
  dilemma is the backbone from mid-September; if not, revert"). These become next
  week's §0 obligations, so make them answerable.
- **§11 · Queue state** — headed **NOT SUBMITTED** unless the operator asked.
  State what `status='pending'` currently holds, the validation line (rows,
  strictly increasing, clear of the previous tail, no URLs), the budget, the
  pillar split, then the table **generated by `validate.py`** — never retyped.

Close with a `*Sources: …*` italic footer naming every harvest with n and
timestamp, every web source with its date, and the novelty window.

---

## The per-post entry

```
**23:48 — D1 · CHALLENGE BOARD · NIGHT** *(US East 16:48)*
> Name one thing you have already stopped doing because an agent does it now.
>
> Not better. Just does it.

`seed: "Mine: reading stack traces. I paste and scroll to the fix. I could still do it, and I notice I'd be slower at it than I was in March, which is a sentence I don't fully know what to do with."`

`stream D · 102 chars · latch: "Not better. Just does it."`

> Rationale: what this post is doing mechanically, why it is in this slot, and
> what the seed is for. Two to four sentences. Name the device, not the vibe.
```

Rules for the entry:

- **Time first, then tag, then stream.** Mark `· NIGHT` on the 23:xx and 02:xx
  slots and add the US East local time in italics for those two — that is the
  reason they exist.
- The post body is a blockquote, **one proposition per line, blank `>` between**.
  This is the shape it will have on X and it is how the operator proofreads it.
- The annotation line is always `` `stream <X> · <n> chars · <descriptor>` `` where
  the descriptor is `latch: "…"`, `peg: <dated event>`, `pillar: builder-51`, or a
  short mechanism note. **The char count comes from `validate.py`, never from
  counting by hand.**
- The rationale earns its place by being falsifiable. "Everyone has an answer and
  every answer is arguable" is a claim. "Punchy and relatable" is not.
- Manual slots appear as `**14:00 — YOURS (manual)**` with nothing under them.

**Flagships** — the 02:3x post of each day, and the best slot of the week — get a
bolded lead in the rationale (`**Flagship.**`, `**Highest ceiling in the set.**`,
`**The closer, and the thesis of the set.**`) and a longer justification. If every
post reads equally important, the operator can't triage when the day goes wrong.
